## Verdict and scope

**Amazon SES is the user-approved newsletter/bulk delivery provider (2026-10-25).**
Cloudflare continues to own new scheduling, Queues and dispatch compute; Email
Service remains an option for existing transactional mail only. Its marketing
restriction no longer blocks the selected newsletter architecture.

AWS documents [marketing email](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/) and
[third-party sending authorization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/sending-authorization.html).
This establishes a documented product fit, not live account enablement or blanket
approval of any customer content. Sender consent, AWS policies, regional production
access, identity authority and deliverability controls still apply. No sends or
production writes are authorized or performed in this update.

This is Phase 1 provider feasibility, following the
[design draft PR #6719](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/pull/6719).
It adds research, nonproduction catalog request fixtures and a finite loopback
verification tool. It creates no product routes, tables, subscriptions, Workers,
DNS records, provider products or deployed configuration. Research was checked
2026-10-25; account access and hosted acceptance remain separate evidence.

## Superseded Cloudflare sending option — retained evidence

| Question | Verified public source | Conclusion / missing evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does sending exist? | [Email Service overview](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/) and [REST guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/api/send-emails/rest-api/) | Email Sending beta supports `POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send`, native Workers binding and SMTP. A documented endpoint does not establish this account's permission. |
| Is newsletter marketing allowed? | [FAQ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/faq/) and [Developer Platform terms, Cloudflare Email Service](https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-developer-platform/) | Transactional-only. Terms restrict sends to responses to specific customer interactions facilitating an agreed transaction/update. Opt-in alone does not establish marketing permission. |
| Can a customer authorize its domain? | [Service terms](https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-developer-platform/) | Domains/addresses may be owned or explicitly authorized. SPF/DKIM verification and possible identity/address/script restrictions still apply. This is not a resale or cross-account delegation approval. |
| What DNS/account model is documented? | [Get started](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/get-started/send-emails/) and [domain configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/configuration/domains/) | Cloudflare DNS; onboarding selects a domain in the account. The SMTP guide binds sender domain to the token-owning account. No reviewed evidence establishes arbitrary external DNS or customer zones staying in independent accounts while a platform token sends. |
| What domain records are needed? | [Domain configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/configuration/domains/) | Provider-configured SPF, DKIM, DMARC and bounce-routing MX, with a `cf-bounce` return path. Preserve customer root MX and existing DMARC. Do not change DNS during this research. |
| What are content/account limits? | [Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) | 50 combined recipients, 5 MiB message, 16 KB custom headers; 30 combined routing/sending domains per zone. Account daily capacity scales by reputation; no universal fixed daily quota is documented. Need account-specific capacity before selling aggregate workspace limits. |
| Is sending isolated by a universal sandbox? | [Service terms](https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-developer-platform/) and [local development](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/observability/local-development/sending/) | Provider can impose restricted sandbox volume/destinations; local Worker simulation exists. Neither proves a universally available isolated hosted email sandbox or legal eligibility. Never use a remote binding believing it is a simulation. |
| What does it cost? | [Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/pricing/) | Workers Paid arbitrary-recipient sending: 3,000/account/billing-month included, then $0.35/1,000; accepted hard bounces count. Verified-destination sends are free but are not a substitute for arbitrary-recipient account acceptance. |
| Are feedback and suppressions supported? | [Event subscriptions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/event-subscriptions/) and [suppression management](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/configuration/suppressions/) | Sending-domain delivery/bounce/complaint facts can reach Queues; provider suppressions exist. Need hosted event binding and no-plaintext retention compatibility proof. |
| Can unknown sends be replayed safely? | [REST guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/api/send-emails/rest-api/) | No provider idempotency guarantee established by the inspected guide. Preserve unknown submission and reconcile; no blind automatic resend. |

This table explains the rejected bulk-sending option; it is not a request to
obtain a Cloudflare marketing exception. No provider contact was sent. Existing
Cloudflare transactional transports remain governed by their own limits and terms.

## SES feasibility and remaining acceptance

| Boundary | Verified source and conclusion | Unverified live evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sending API | [SES v2 SendEmail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/APIReference-V2/API_SendEmail.html) supports simple/raw/templated messages. Reuse the existing `packages/email-service` SES adapter; qualify its Worker boundary and unsubscribe headers. | Actual account/region IAM, configuration set, message identity and adapter/runtime acceptance. |
| Customer domains | [Create/verify identities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/creating-identities.html): publish SES DKIM records in customer DNS. [Sending authorization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/sending-authorization.html) also documents customer-owned identity delegation to a third-party sender. | Chosen platform-account or delegated identity model, ownership proof and least-privilege policies. No mandatory Cloudflare DNS transfer. |
| Return path | [Custom MAIL FROM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/mail-from.html) uses a dedicated subdomain with SPF/MX; preserve root MX and customer DMARC. | Aligned DKIM/SPF, identity region, fallback policy and independently approved sender. |
| Capacity | [SES sandbox](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/request-production-access.html): per-region restrictions, verified recipients, 200 messages/24 hours and one/second. [Quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/manage-sending-quotas.html) include rolling 24-hour volume and rate. | Regional production access and aggregate capacity for all workspaces; application local-day quota is a separate ceiling. |
| Feedback | [SES event notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/monitor-sending-activity-using-notifications.html): configuration-set publishing including SNS; authenticated bounded ingestion into Cloudflare Queues. | Topic/configuration-set identity, SNS signature verification, event-to-workspace mapping, suppression handling and retention compatibility. |
| Policy and safety | SES product fit does not waive consent, spam/abuse policy, workspace/domain/sender approval, quota, full-campaign reservation or stop fence. | Independent security review and hosted release acceptance; no sends in this task. |

## Approved newsletter tier contract

The user clarified that a workspace has exactly one newsletter tier:

| Tier | Price | Daily allowance | Billing-period allowance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | 10 only after workspace newsletter approval; otherwise 0 | No separate monthly pool |
| Tier 1 | $2/month | At most 200 | 2,000 total |
| Tier 2 | $10/month | 500 | No separate monthly pool |

No extra free allowance on paid tiers. Tier 1 exhaustion blocks sending until the
next verified period. Workspace-local midnight defines quota days; authoritative
subscription anniversaries define Tier 1 pool periods. A coupon can discount a
product without changing its tier. Both paid catalog entries belong to the same
exclusive newsletter group, independently of the workspace's base subscription.

[SES pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/) lists à la carte $0.10/1,000
and first-band Essentials $0.16/1,000. Email-only Tier 1 cost is $0.20/$0.32;
full 31-day Tier 2 is $1.55/$2.48. Actual account plan, data, optional features,
Cloudflare, storage and payment costs remain unverified/excluded; these are not
net margins. The old Cloudflare $0.35/1,000 estimate is superseded for newsletters.

The user approved #6719's retention and billing policies as written on 2026-10-25,
including full-campaign quota reservation, grace and downgrade handling. All
unapproved workspaces have **zero newsletter sends**, regardless of tier/payment.
Free grants 10/day only after newsletter approval. Domain/sender approvals remain
separate. A quota admission can be all-or-nothing, but external delivery cannot:
bounces, unsubscribes, outages and Stop still require honest partial outcomes.
Platform-wide GDPR/PDPD implementation is a separate lane; cite the approved
newsletter retention standard in #6719 without expanding this feasibility task.

## Reproducible local proof

The checked-in SDK is `@polar-sh/sdk` 0.49.0. Current upstream
[product API examples](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/products/create) use a
versioned contract; do not copy new SDK constructors into this repository without
qualification. The fixtures deliberately serialize through the installed SDK.
No dependency change is needed.

From the repository root:

```bash
node scripts/verification/newsletter-polar-webhook-proof.mjs
```

The tool validates two draft monthly product requests in
`scripts/verification/newsletter-polar-sandbox-products.json`: $2 (200 minor units)
and $10 (1,000 minor units), with fixed USD prices and exclusive-tier metadata.
This proves serialization, not product creation or entitlement enforcement.

It then starts an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` HTTP receiver, generates a random in-memory
fixture signing key and posts eight finite requests. The real installed Polar
`validateEvent` checks the raw body and Standard Webhooks headers. Expected results:

- Valid signed `product.created` returns 200 and a parsed product.
- Identical signed replay returns 200 without another in-memory effect.
- Modified body, missing signature, expired timestamp and wrong key return 401.
- Correctly signed wrong-organization event returns 403.
- Reusing the signed event ID with changed content returns 409.

The listener closes after the proof and prints only PASS summaries. It does not
read credential files, load `.env`, call Polar/Cloudflare, expose a network service,
print signing material, or persist customer data. Receiver state is in memory;
it is not production webhook code or durable billing idempotency. This proof does
not exercise the Pay adapter, real subscription lifecycle or hosted webhook delivery.

Observed locally: SDK request serialization and all eight HTTP cases passed.
Keep exact-commit CI lint/type/test/build gates distinct from this executed proof.

## Polar sandbox continuation

[Polar sandbox](https://polar.sh/docs/integrate/sandbox) has separate organization,
API host and credentials. The next authenticated operation must explicitly target
`sandbox-api.polar.sh`, with no fallback to live mode. Product creation needs
`products:write`; listing/readback needs the corresponding read access.

1. Supply a sandbox organization token through the private secret mechanism. Use
   `POLAR_SANDBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` in an authorized execution environment; use
   `POLAR_SANDBOX_ORGANIZATION_ID` to pin the target, not browser input. Never log
   the token, request Authorization headers or raw provider responses.
2. Confirm the sandbox organization with bounded read-only access. List existing
   test products with a bounded page budget; match an owned run marker and exact
   product/price/metadata before deciding to create anything.
3. Create exactly two draft products from the serialized fixtures, bound to that
   sandbox organization. Keep an operation journal before each external write.
   No automatic create retry: unknown outcome requires marker-based reconciliation
   and readback before any next create. Record private product/price IDs and prices.
4. Register or reuse a sandbox-only webhook receiver. Follow
   [Polar local webhook forwarding](https://polar.sh/docs/integrate/cli/webhooks)
   with a sandbox organization. The official listener prints its local signing
   secret: capture it privately into `POLAR_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, never into
   tool output, PR artifacts or chat. Use a secure executor, not a public terminal
   log containing the banner.
5. Verify genuine product-created events through the installed raw-body validator,
   including organization/product binding; repeat tamper/replay/expired controls.
   Synthetic `polar webhook trigger` is explicitly separate from genuine events.
6. Stop the local listener, remove only owned ephemeral forwarding resources and
   retain redacted receipts. Do not delete a test product with an unknown outcome.

## Credential and no-send boundary

No live SES/Polar checks are part of this update. The earlier run had no usable
sandbox credential and created no provider products or hosted webhook receipts.
Do not read credential files, print tokens or infer production domain readiness
from checked-in Mail configuration. Stop before any authenticated check until
credentials are supplied privately via `request_secret` (file delivery for an
approved shell executor where supported), never chat.

SES read-only checks need `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and
`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` for temporary credentials, plus pinned `AWS_REGION`, account
ID, identity ARN/domain and configuration-set name. Prefer short-lived least-
privilege read-only credentials; no `ses:SendEmail` or provisioning authority is
needed for account/identity inspection. Polar sandbox needs
`POLAR_SANDBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `POLAR_SANDBOX_ORGANIZATION_ID` and, for genuine local
webhook validation, `POLAR_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Refer only to variable names
in public artifacts. The authenticated continuation above remains unexecuted.

No own-domain send proof is attempted: **no sends and no production writes** is
the current custody boundary, including SES sandbox/simulator sends. A later
separately authorized proof must pin a disposable identity/account/region, preserve
unknown-send fences, and satisfy the existing
[Cloudflare cost/stop rules](/build/development-tools/oxc-cloudflare-adoption#runaway-work-and-cost-acceptance)
for queue/dispatch compute. Provider selection does not authorize that proof.

acceptance and sandbox mutations remain blocked, not complete. Neither draft PR
